column2: Someone who stares at a float for hours and calls it a proper holiday.
A deep, menacing sound made by a lion, a sports car engine or someone whose toe you just stepped on.
A brisk harness-racing horse for whom a leisurely stroll is practically an insult.
A simple bar that lifts heavy loads with minimal effort — physics in the service of cleverness, and Archimedes' favourite toy.
A tiny tumbler for strong spirits — glassware with a short, eventful evening ahead of it.
Tiny wavelets dancing across water after a breeze or a skimmed pebble.
The long ankle-length robe worn by Orthodox clergy — not to be confused with an everyday dressing gown.
A tiny floating plant capable of turning an entire garden pond into a green carpet overnight.
A burial cloth — the one garment you never have to iron twice.
A sprawling tale of families, heroes and feuds too big to fit inside a single volume.
A patch of trees and flowerbeds where you work hard all weekend just to sit in the shade.
A mesh bag trailing in the water to hold caught fish — temporary accommodation with questionable room service.
Black powdery residue left behind whenever a fire decides not to tidy up after itself.
A hefty freshwater fish capable of putting an angler's patience through a rigorous exam.
A steppe antelope with a remarkably bulbous nose — looking as though it arrived slightly late to a beauty pageant.
A traditional stone dwelling of the Caucasus mountains, built as if it grew straight out of the cliffside.
A brass woodwind instrument with a soulful voice, sounding as though jazz is telling a personal secret.
A bowl of tossed leaves and vegetables — culinary proof that greens can get along.
Explosive rockets lighting up the night sky — guaranteed to make adults say 'ooh' like toddlers.
The masculine sex in the animal kingdom, fulfilling its biological role with varying levels of enthusiasm.
The feminine sex in nature, usually stuck with the lion's share of looking after the kids.
A winged metal tube with jet engines — basically a flying bus that asks you to fasten your seatbelt.
A heavy lorry with a hinged bed that unloads gravel without anyone picking up a shovel.
An elevated clerical title or position of authority rarely handed out merely for a nice smile.
A military engineer specialising in clearing mines — someone for whom 'watch your step' is never a joke.
A humble garden outbuilding storing everything from spades to mysterious boxes kept 'just in case'.
A wood-lined steam room where people pay good money to sweat profusely and call it relaxation.
Sweet white crystals that make tea friendlier while keeping dentists firmly in business.
Leather straps and fittings for hitching a horse — a wardrobe worn strictly for work, not fashion.
The business of moving goods off shelves — the happy moment a product finally meets a wallet.
A stout timber or concrete post driven deep into the ground — a building's long-legged foundation.
Electromagnetic brightness that lets you see the furniture — sorely missed the second a fuse blows.
A three-eyed roadside junction boss dedicated to testing the patience of drivers and pedestrians alike.
A shrill, high-pitched note produced by pursed lips, a referee or an impatient kettle.
An arched stone ceiling holding up a roof in quiet defiance of gravity.
A relative connected by marriage — the sort of extended family member easiest explained with a diagram.
A link between people, devices or events — always dropping right as your train enters a tunnel.
The joint where a pipe, road or elbow changes direction — geometry meeting flexibility.
Coins handed back at the till, or a shift in plans — one word carrying two entirely different anxieties.
A slight movement in position — either welcome progress or a sign your bookcase is leaning.
Rich, buttery baked dough that clearly enjoyed a very generous upbringing.
A scheduled block of time at the cinema, clinic or pub — strictly bounded by the clock.
Scattering seeds into prepared soil — the optimistic opening act of the farming calendar.
The compass point your needle reliably seeks, where winter loves showing off its character.
A shaped leather seat strapped to a horse — rarely chosen for plush armchair comfort.
Someone perched astride a horse — a passenger travelling without the benefit of a seatbelt.
One of the four quarters of the year, or the brief window when a hobby gets its starring role.
A heavy, lockable steel cabinet for valuables — and occasionally the spare key to the safe itself.
The intimate side of romance and biology — a topic for which polite adults invent endless euphemisms.
A closed religious or ideological group with rigid beliefs — best viewed with a healthy dose of scepticism.
A trace chemical element vital for health in tiny doses — proof that moderation really matters.
A small rural settlement where the high street knows your business faster than social media.
A fast, destructive torrent of mountain mud and boulders — best admired from a very safe postcode.
A prized, pink-fleshed fish famous for leaping up waterfalls and gracing festive dinner tables.
The close circle bound by blood or marriage who still remember you before any of your achievements.
A tiny botanical time capsule containing everything required to build a tree.
The upper legislative chamber in several countries, where debates move at a stately pace.
Sun-dried meadow grass baled for winter livestock — basically summer neatly packed into stacks.
A bright yellow non-metal famous in chemistry labs and notorious for smelling like rotten eggs.
A member of the South Slavic nation native to Serbia and the Balkans.
A single instalment of a television drama — always followed by 'just one more before bed'.
A curved, hand-held blade used since antiquity to reap grain by hand.
An open mesh of knotted cord built to catch fish, stop footballs or tangle in the shed.
An interconnected web of nodes or channels — equally capable of landing fish or eating your evening online.
A crisp alcoholic drink brewed from fermented apples — orchard fruit with weekend ambitions.
The power to resist force — whether lifting weights or resisting the fridge at midnight.
A powerhouse of muscle to whom stubborn jam jars surrender without negotiation.
Fermented green fodder stored airtight for winter cattle — farm food with a pungent personality.
A formal council of senior church officials gathered to settle ecclesiastical matters.
A thick, sugary liquid capable of convincing plain tap water it's actually a pudding.
An orderly set of rules and parts designed to make chaos look vaguely organised.
A long-necked Indian lute with shimmering strings that sounds like a doorway to another dimension.
A lightweight, plain-woven cotton fabric familiar from summer dresses and vintage aprons.
A fine wire-mesh kitchen strainer separating smooth flour from lumps and wheat from chaff.
A traditional story told in lively folk style, rich with colourful turns of phrase.
A young outdoors enthusiast mastering camping, knot-tying and lighting fires without matches.
A leafy urban park pocket offering a breath of fresh air amidst an ocean of tarmac.
A wooden deck on four urethane wheels demanding balance and a healthy respect for concrete.
A short comic scene or rapid pencil drawing — a bright idea in travel-sized format.
A small, secluded monastic community where silence is treated as the most respected neighbour.
An underground stone burial chamber — real estate with remarkably permanent tenants.
The tilted flank of a hill or mountain, built for sledging in winter and panting in summer.
A fish-hunting bird of prey — a feathered angler equipped with its own wings and talons.
Domesticated farm animals grouped together so nobody has to count every cow and sheep individually.
Transparent sticky tape — the office superhero temporarily repairing nearly everything.
The restless state where nothing holds your interest and the wall clock starts ticking in slow motion.
A striped North American mammal armed with a famously unforgettable chemical defence system.
An impression left in mud or snow — forensic evidence left behind by even the most careful walker.
A salty droplet escaping the eye during grief, laughter or onion chopping.
Informal, playful street vocabulary that grammar textbooks always catch up with ten years too late.
A juicy, purple-skinned stone fruit destined for jam jars, crumbles and sticky fingers.
The richest, fattiest layer of milk — adored by coffee and feared by January diets.
A thick, slippery secretion — a word guaranteed to ruin anyone's appetite at dinner.
A single unit of language carrying meaning — tiny enough to type, powerful enough to start or end a row.
A distinct horizontal sheet or stratum — delicious inside a sponge cake, historical inside a cliff.
A household attendant from an era when the social ladder was extraordinarily steep.
An unverified piece of gossip — what happens when ears hear half a story and imagination writes the rest.
A shiny silicate mineral that splits effortlessly into paper-thin transparent flakes.
Watery fluid in the mouth kicking off digestion before your fork even reaches the plate.
A scheduled stretch of factory or hospital work, or the moment one crew hands the baton to the next.
A violent, spinning funnel of wind — an atmospheric dance best watched from a sturdy cellar.
A fierce snowstorm with howling winds that buries footpaths and weekend travel plans alike.
A blend of different ingredients — the outcome of every 'let's throw it all in together' experiment.
Thick, polluted city fog — urban air that clearly forgot to run the extractor fan.
An overpowering, foul odour that sends even houseflies searching for the fire exit.
A chaotic period of political upheaval when history refuses to march in a straight line.
The underlying point or message — desperately sought halfway through flat-pack furniture instructions.
Frozen white ice crystals falling from winter clouds — magical in December, slushy misery by March.
Someone who looks down their nose at ordinary tastes and judges people by their wine cellar.
A neat bundle of cut grain stalks tied together at harvest time.
A female relative by marriage — another knot in the extended family tree.
Man's loyal four-legged best friend, greeting you at the door as if you'd survived a polar expedition.
A wide-eyed nocturnal bird of prey — the universal mascot of wisdom and staying up far too late.
An opinion on what you ought to do — a free commodity generously handed out whether you asked or not.
A flat, handled scoop serving as a broom's loyal sidekick in the endless war against crumbs.
Bicarbonate powder kept in the kitchen cupboard as a baker's secret weapon and universal stain remover.
A bold woodland crow sporting bright flash-blue wing feathers and a remarkably loud voice.
A recognised pattern of stars — ancient humanity's favourite game of cosmic join-the-dots.
Liquid squeezed from ripe fruit or vegetables — the lazy way to get vitamins without chewing an apple.
The blazing star warming our planet — Earth's primary lamp, happily lacking an off switch.
A large, herbivorous tropical lizard with a spiky crest and a permanently unimpressed expression.
A spotted African scavenger notorious for its eerie, human-like giggling call.
A classic white painkiller tablet fondly remembered the morning after a slightly too successful party.
Scotland's national bard and folk-song collector who gave the world 'Auld Lang Syne'.
The archetypal grey-bearded wizard of Middle-earth, inspired by old Norse and British folklore.
